0.
0.1 This Indian

FOREWORD

Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 31 January 1977, after the draft finalized by the Packaging of Engineering Goods Sectional Committee had been approved by the Marine, Cargo Movement and Packaging Division Council. 0.2 Sewing machines are precision machines, which unless packed properly may sustain damage. At present there exist a few modes of packaging In order to these machines for both inland transport as well as for export. establish a uniform pattern of packaging for surface transport as well as to ensure proper protection of the contents of the package, it has been felt necessary to formulate this code. 0.3 In preparing this standard, assistance has been derived from JIS Z 0705 : 1960 Packaging of household sewing machines for export, issued by the Japanese Industrial Standards Committee.

a) head assembly comprising of all parts except the base or table assembly and stand sub-assembly but including the accessory box and the hand attachment ( if supplied with the head ); b) base, cover or table components/sub-assemblies; c) stand components/sub-assemblies. 3.1.3 Sewing machines shall be packed boxes, in either of the following: and

3.2.1 Unit packing of the head assembly, base, cover, table, sub-assembly shall be such as to prevent dust, moisture, etc, entering by use of suitable packing materials as provided in 4.1. 3.2.2 The head assembly and the accessories shall be held the packing boxes to avoid shifting during transportation. firmly

3.2.3 In case the head assembly/accessories are packed in corrugated fibreboard boxes, the flaps shall be closed by gummed paper tape or any Alternatively, the flaps may be stapled. other suitable material. 3.2.4 The boxes/cases shall be strapped properly.

3.2.5 An anti-rust protection shall be given to the head assembly either at the time of packing, or at any stage of its manufacture, prior to packing. 3.2.6 All transit. loose parts shall be suitably wrapped to avoid packing damage also. in

5. SAMPLING

AND TESTING

5.1 Sampling - Representative samples of the packed boxes shall be drawn from the lot for testing. The sampling plan shall be as agreed between the purchaser and the supplier. 5.2 Testing - The packed box shall be subjected as per the requirements prescribed: a) RoZling Test to the following type tests

as per IS : 7028 (Part V)-1973".

b) Drop Test-to be tested for drop resistance on all six sides as well as on all corner of the box from a height of 1 metre in accordance with the procedure in IS : 7028 (Part IV)-19747. c) Stack Load Test - as given in IS : 7028 (Part I)-1973:. The number of similar boxes/cases above the case under test shall be such as ( keeping in view the maximum heights admissible in transportation by various modes ) to obtain a total height of: 1) 2 metres for corrugated boxes, and cases. 2) 4 metres for wooden
*Performance tperformance drop test. fperformance

packing

tests for complete, filled transport packages: Part V Rolling test. tests for complete, filled transport packages: Part IV Vertical impact tests for complete, filled transport packages: Part I Stack load test.

b) there is no physical damage machine or on the components; c) electrical 6. MARKING connections,

if any, are intact.
